core_obligations: Choose a nonzero element x of the ideal J and use that the fraction field extension is algebraic to write down a polynomial relation for x with coefficients a_0, ..., a_d in A, both extreme coefficients nonzero (proof lines 6187-6190).
Solve the relation for the constant term: it is divisible by x and therefore lies in the ideal, which gives a nonzero element of A inside J (proof lines 6190-6191).
Read the geometric conclusion off the algebraic one, that a proper closed subset of the spectrum of B has image that is not dense (statement lines 6182-6183).
proof_roadmap: Take a nonzero element of the ideal and turn its algebraicity into a polynomial relation over A with nonzero constant term (proof lines 6186-6190).
Observe that the constant term is a nonzero element of A inside the ideal (proof lines 6190-6192).
difficulty_reason: For an inclusion of domains A contained in B inducing an algebraic extension of fraction fields, the lemma states that every nonzero ideal of B meets A nontrivially, hence that images of proper closed subsets of the spectrum of B are not dense (statement lines 6178-6184). The proof does not use integrality of B over A or a norm argument: it takes a nonzero element x of the ideal, converts its algebraicity into a polynomial relation with coefficients in A and a nonzero constant term, and observes that the constant term is divisible by x and therefore lies in the ideal (proof lines 6186-6192). The choice of the constant term as the witness is the step that carries the content. H2.
